\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{വൈകാതെ} (vaikāte)}{വൈകാതെ (vaikāte)}]{\ml{വൈകാതെ} (vaikāte) — before long}

\label{lesson:ML-C359-vaikate}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for following that, then the Malayalam for throughout.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വൈകാതെ}}
\textbf{\ml{വൈകാതെ}} — \emph{vaikāte} — \textquotedblleft{}before long\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വൈകാതെ} \ml{ആംബുലൻസ്} \ml{എത്തി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vaikāte āmbulansŭ etti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Before long the ambulance arrived.
\end{quote}

The negative form of \ml{വൈകുക}, to be late: without being late.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{വൈകാതെ}} (\emph{vaikāte}) is native Dravidian, the negative participle of \ml{വൈകുക} (\emph{vaikuka}), \textquotedblleft{}to stay, to be late\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 5554): without delaying.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vaikāte}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vaikāte}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vaikāte āmbulansŭ etti.} — Before long the ambulance arrived.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for following that, then the Malayalam for throughout, then say \emph{vaikāte} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{വൈകാതെ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Before long\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഒടുക്കം} (oṭukkaṁ)}{ഒടുക്കം (oṭukkaṁ)}]{\ml{ഒടുക്കം} (oṭukkaṁ) — in the end; the end}

\label{lesson:ML-C359-otukkam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for throughout, then the Malayalam for before long.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഒടുക്കം}}
\textbf{\ml{ഒടുക്കം}} — \emph{oṭukkaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}in the end; the end\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഒടുക്കം} \ml{അവർ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{പരിഹാരം} \ml{കണ്ടെത്തി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{oṭukkaṁ avar oru parihāraṁ kaṇṭetti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the end they found a solution.
\end{quote}

Also a noun: \ml{കഥയുടെ} \ml{ഒടുക്കം}, the end of the story.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഒടുക്കം}} (\emph{oṭukkaṁ}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 954 lists Malayalam \emph{oṭukkam}, \textquotedblleft{}the end; finally\textquotedblright{}, beside \ml{ഒടുങ്ങുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to come to an end\textquotedblright{}. \ml{ഒടുവിൽ}, \textquotedblleft{}at last\textquotedblright{}, comes from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oṭukkaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oṭukkaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{oṭukkaṁ avar oru parihāraṁ kaṇṭetti.} — In the end they found a solution.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for throughout, then the Malayalam for before long, then say \emph{oṭukkaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഏതാണ്ട്} (ētāṇṭŭ)}{ഏതാണ്ട് (ētāṇṭŭ)}]{\ml{ഏതാണ്ട്} (ētāṇṭŭ) — nearly; roughly}

\label{lesson:ML-C359-etantu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for before long, then the Malayalam for in the end.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഏതാണ്ട്}}
\textbf{\ml{ഏതാണ്ട്}} — \emph{ētāṇṭŭ} — \textquotedblleft{}nearly; roughly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ഗ്രാമം} \ml{ഏതാണ്ട്} \ml{മുഴുവൻ} \ml{വെള്ളത്തിൽ} \ml{ആയിരുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{grāmaṁ ētāṇṭŭ muḻuvan veḷḷattil āyirunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The village was nearly all under water.
\end{quote}

Before a number it means about: \ml{ഏതാണ്ട്} \ml{നൂറ്} \ml{ആളുകൾ}, about a hundred people.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഏതാണ്ട്}} (\emph{ētāṇṭŭ}) is a native Malayalam adverb whose origin is not settled. It softens a number or a statement: almost, roughly.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ētāṇṭŭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ētāṇṭŭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{grāmaṁ ētāṇṭŭ muḻuvan veḷḷattil āyirunnu.} — The village was nearly all under water.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for before long, then the Malayalam for in the end, then say \emph{ētāṇṭŭ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഇടയ്ക്കിടെ} (iṭaykkiṭe)}{ഇടയ്ക്കിടെ (iṭaykkiṭe)}]{\ml{ഇടയ്ക്കിടെ} (iṭaykkiṭe) — now and then}

\label{lesson:ML-C359-itaykkite}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for in the end, then the Malayalam for nearly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഇടയ്ക്കിടെ}}
\textbf{\ml{ഇടയ്ക്കിടെ}} — \emph{iṭaykkiṭe} — \textquotedblleft{}now and then\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അവൻ} \ml{ഇടയ്ക്കിടെ} \ml{മുത്തശ്ശിയെ} \ml{കാണാൻ} \ml{പോകും}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avan iṭaykkiṭe muttaśśiye kāṇān pōkuṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He goes to see grandmother now and then.
\end{quote}

\ml{ഇട}, an interval, said twice: at one interval after another.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഇടയ്ക്കിടെ}} (\emph{iṭaykkiṭe}) is native Dravidian, built by repeating \ml{ഇട} (\emph{iṭa}), \textquotedblleft{}an interval, a space between\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 448), the word inside \ml{ഇടയിൽ}, \textquotedblleft{}between\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṭaykkiṭe}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṭaykkiṭe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avan iṭaykkiṭe muttaśśiye kāṇān pōkuṁ.} — He goes to see grandmother now and then.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for in the end, then the Malayalam for nearly, then say \emph{iṭaykkiṭe} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{തൊട്ടുപിന്നാലെ} (toṭṭupinnāle)}{തൊട്ടുപിന്നാലെ (toṭṭupinnāle)}]{\ml{തൊട്ടുപിന്നാലെ} (toṭṭupinnāle) — right after; close behind}

\label{lesson:ML-C359-tottupinnale}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for nearly, then the Malayalam for now and then.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{തൊട്ടുപിന്നാലെ}}
\textbf{\ml{തൊട്ടുപിന്നാലെ}} — \emph{toṭṭupinnāle} — \textquotedblleft{}right after; close behind\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ആംബുലൻസിന്റെ} \ml{തൊട്ടുപിന്നാലെ} \ml{പോലീസ്} \ml{എത്തി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āmbulansinṟe toṭṭupinnāle pōlīsŭ etti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police arrived right after the ambulance.
\end{quote}

\ml{തൊട്ട്}, touching, + \ml{പിന്നാലെ}, behind: so close behind as to touch.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{തൊട്ടുപിന്നാലെ}} (\emph{toṭṭupinnāle}) is a native Dravidian compound of \ml{തൊട്ട്} (\emph{toṭṭŭ}), \textquotedblleft{}touching\textquotedblright{}, from \ml{തൊടുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to touch\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3480), and \ml{പിന്നാലെ} (\emph{pinnāle}), \textquotedblleft{}behind, after\textquotedblright{}, from \ml{പിൻ} (DEDR 4205).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{toṭṭupinnāle}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āmbulansinṟe toṭṭupinnāle pōlīsŭ etti.} — The police arrived right after the ambulance.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for nearly, then the Malayalam for now and then, then say \emph{toṭṭupinnāle} again
\end{itemize}
